newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Goodale regrets grain delays to Japan.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Goodale regrets grain delays to Japan.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said Monday he would give his regrets to Japan for delayed grain shipments from Vancouver, but he said the delays did not necessarily cause a loss of sales.

"I will obviously be talking to the Japanese about grain transportation and that we very sincerely regret the disruptions that have occurred during this particularly harsh winter season and we are pulling out all the stops to overcome those difficulties," Goodale told reporters before leaving on a 10-day trade mission to Japan and Indonesia.
Heavy snow, extreme cold and equipment failure led to delays in rail shipments to Pacific ports since early January.
The Canadian Wheat Board faces more than C$15 million in demurrage fines and has acknowledged deferring sales.

"I have no hard evidence before me at the moment that there's been an absolute loss of sales. Deferral, yes, of one period of delivery to another and certainly the risk of a loss of sales, but I hope we're getting our arms around this situation fast enough to avoid a loss of volume to the Japanese market," Goodale added.
Goodale said he spoke on Friday to the presidents of Canadian National Railway Co and Canadian Pacific unit CP Rail System about expediting grain movement.
There were 3,433 grain and oilseed railcars unloaded in Vancouver in the week ended March 9 compared to a target of 3,400, CWB spokeswoman Rhea Yates said.
Prince Rupert railcar unloads, however, totalled 1,299 hopper cars compared to a weekly target of 1,500, Yates said.
